1. Problem Statement

A 4-bit game score (0–15) is set on switches S3–S0. When START is pressed, the score is sampled and classified. A Moore FSM keeps the result on one indicator LED until ACK is pressed, and then returns to IDLE. RESET (synchronous, active-high) returns the system to IDLE at any time. Modification H1 replaces the three base categories with four:

Score (Dec)Score[3:0]CategoryLED
0 – 40000 – 0100LOWGreen
5 – 80101 – 1000MEDIUMYellow
9 – 121001 – 1100HIGHRed
13 – 151101 – 1111EXCELLENTBlue

2. Requirements and Assumptions

  • Moore FSM, 5 states (IDLE, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, EXCELLENT), 3-bit binary encoding.
  • IDLE → category state on START; category state → IDLE on ACK; RESET forces IDLE.
  • The 4-bit input register loads the switches on every clock while in IDLE and holds its value in every other state.
  • START and switch changes are ignored outside IDLE; ACK has no effect in IDLE.
  • Unused codes 101, 110, 111 return to IDLE on the next clock.
  • All 16 inputs are valid (unsigned score), so no error state is needed.
SignalDirWidthDescription
Scorein4Score from switches
STARTin1Sample score, leave IDLE
ACKin1Return to IDLE
Resetin1Synchronous, active-high
Clockin1System clock
LED_LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH / EXCELLENTout1 eachCategory indicators

3. Architecture

The datapath contains the input register and the combinational range decoder. The controller is a Moore FSM: a 3-bit state register, next-state logic and output logic. Distinctive feature: an optimised Logisim implementation in which the input register is one 4-bit Register component and the outputs come from one 3-to-8 decoder on the state (43 gates and 7 flip-flops reduced to 23 gates, 3 flip-flops, one register and one decoder). Unused state codes return to IDLE.

Range decoder (comparators)

Three 4-bit unsigned comparators compare the registered score with the constants 4, 8 and 12:

ComparatorConditionOutput
C1Score > 4GT4
C2Score > 8GT8
C3Score > 12GT12

L = GT4' (0–4)   M = GT4·GT8' (5–8)   H = GT8·GT12' (9–12)   E = GT12 (13–15)

000 IDLE0XX0000000

000 IDLE1XE1000000

010 MEDIUMX0 / 1X010 / 0000100

D2 = RESET'·[IDLE·START·E + Q2·Q1'·Q0'·ACK']
D1 = RESET'·[IDLE·START·(M+H) + Q2'·Q1·ACK']
D0 = RESET'·[IDLE·START·(L+H) + Q2'·Q0·ACK']
Outputs: GREEN = Q2'Q1'Q0, YELLOW = Q2'Q1Q0', RED = Q2'Q1Q0, BLUE = Q2Q1'Q0'

5. Logisim Implementation

Logisim Evolution 5.0.0, file 02_FSM_Logisim/Game_Score_Categorizer.circ. The circuit uses one 4-bit Register (input register, Enable = IDLE), 3 D flip-flops for the state, three 4-bit unsigned Comparators, one 3-to-8 Decoder for the outputs and 23 basic gates, arranged left to right as inputs, inverters, input register, range decoder, next-state logic, state register, output logic and LEDs. A splitter joins S3–S0 into the register input; the register output is the 4-bit bus SCORE, which is compared with constants 4, 8 and 12. The decoder on Q2 Q1 Q0 gives IDLE (output 0) and the four category LEDs (outputs 1–4), replacing the separate output AND gates. All 16 scores were checked with START, hold, ACK and RESET: 16/16 pass.

6. Verilog Implementation

Coding style: parameter state codes, case on Moore_State with begin/end per state and if/else transitions, Moore outputs assigned in every state (no latches), synchronous reset, default to IDLE.

Game_Score_Categorizer.v

`timescale 1ns/1ps
module Game_Score_Categorizer (Score, START, ACK, Clock, Reset,
                               LED_LOW, LED_MEDIUM, LED_HIGH, LED_EXCELLENT);
  input [3:0] Score;
  input START, ACK, Clock, Reset;
  output LED_LOW, LED_MEDIUM, LED_HIGH, LED_EXCELLENT;
  reg LED_LOW, LED_MEDIUM, LED_HIGH, LED_EXCELLENT;

  parameter IDLE = 3'b000, LOW = 3'b001, MEDIUM = 3'b010, HIGH = 3'b011, EXCELLENT = 3'b100;
  reg [2:0] Moore_State;
  reg [3:0] Score_Reg;

  wire Is_Low, Is_Medium, Is_High, Is_Excellent;

  assign Is_Low       = (Score_Reg <= 4'd4);
  assign Is_Medium    = (Score_Reg >= 4'd5)  & (Score_Reg <= 4'd8);
  assign Is_High      = (Score_Reg >= 4'd9)  & (Score_Reg <= 4'd12);
  assign Is_Excellent = (Score_Reg >= 4'd13);

  always
    @ (posedge Clock)
      if (Reset)
        Score_Reg <= 4'b0000;
      else if (Moore_State == IDLE)
        Score_Reg <= Score;
      else
        Score_Reg <= Score_Reg;

  always
    @ (posedge Clock)
      if (Reset)
        Moore_State <= IDLE;
      else
        case (Moore_State)
          IDLE :
            begin
              if (START)
                begin
                  if (Is_Low)
                    Moore_State <= LOW;
                  else if (Is_Medium)
                    Moore_State <= MEDIUM;
                  else if (Is_High)
                    Moore_State <= HIGH;
                  else
                    Moore_State <= EXCELLENT;
                end
              else
                Moore_State <= IDLE;
            end

          LOW :
            begin
              if (ACK)
                Moore_State <= IDLE;
              else
                Moore_State <= LOW;
            end

          MEDIUM :
            begin
              if (ACK)
                Moore_State <= IDLE;
              else
                Moore_State <= MEDIUM;
            end

          HIGH :
            begin
              if (ACK)
                Moore_State <= IDLE;
              else
                Moore_State <= HIGH;
            end

          EXCELLENT :
            begin
              if (ACK)
                Moore_State <= IDLE;
              else
                Moore_State <= EXCELLENT;
            end

          default :
            begin
              Moore_State <= IDLE;
            end
        endcase

  always
    @ (Moore_State)
      case (Moore_State)
        IDLE :
          begin
            LED_LOW = 0;
            LED_MEDIUM = 0;
            LED_HIGH = 0;
            LED_EXCELLENT = 0;
          end

        LOW :
          begin
            LED_LOW = 1;
            LED_MEDIUM = 0;
            LED_HIGH = 0;
            LED_EXCELLENT = 0;
          end

        MEDIUM :
          begin
            LED_LOW = 0;
            LED_MEDIUM = 1;
            LED_HIGH = 0;
            LED_EXCELLENT = 0;
          end

        HIGH :
          begin
            LED_LOW = 0;
            LED_MEDIUM = 0;
            LED_HIGH = 1;
            LED_EXCELLENT = 0;
          end

        EXCELLENT :
          begin
            LED_LOW = 0;
            LED_MEDIUM = 0;
            LED_HIGH = 0;
            LED_EXCELLENT = 1;
          end

        default :
          begin
            LED_LOW = 0;
            LED_MEDIUM = 0;
            LED_HIGH = 0;
            LED_EXCELLENT = 0;
          end
      endcase

endmodule

A button press lasts millions of 100 MHz clocks, but START is ignored outside IDLE and ACK is ignored in IDLE, so each press causes exactly one transition and no debouncer is needed.

10. Challenges and Corrections

IssueCorrection
Loading the score and deciding on the same clock edge would use the old register valueRegister loads continuously in IDLE and freezes when the FSM leaves IDLE
Five states need three bits3-bit state register; unused codes return to IDLE
A button press lasts millions of clocks and bouncesSTART acts only in IDLE and ACK only in a category state, so one press gives one transition
Logisim circuit larger than neededOne 4-bit Register and one 3-to-8 Decoder: 43 gates + 7 FFs reduced to 23 gates + 3 FFs

11. Conclusion

The four-category Game Score Categorizer (H1) was designed as a Moore FSM with a registered datapath and a comparator-based range decoder. The Logisim implementation was verified for all 16 scores, every state, reset, START/ACK sequencing and boundary values. The same design passed 66 of 66 checks in Vivado 2018.3 behavioural simulation, synthesised to 9 LUTs and 9 flip-flops, and was demonstrated on the Boolean board. Limitations: one score per transaction. Future work: 7-segment display of the score, category counters (H4), CHANGE detection (H5).

13. Team Reflection

Keshavraj led the group from the first reading of the problem sheet to the final Pull Request. He set the plan early: agree the H1 ranges and the state encoding first, then build Logisim, Verilog and the FPGA flow on the same design, so every stage could be checked against the one before it. He kept the repository, the STATUS log and the documentation up to date while dividing the work so that each member owned one part: Nandini and Keshavraj the Logisim circuit, Manthan the Verilog, and Palaksh the Vivado and FPGA flow.

The most useful lesson was how much the timing of the input register matters. Loading the score and taking the decision on the same clock edge would have used the old value, so the register loads only in IDLE and freezes once the FSM leaves it. We also learned that a design that works can still be made simpler: under Keshavraj's direction the Logisim circuit was reduced from 43 gates to 23 without changing its behaviour. Working through simulation first and hardware second meant that the board worked the first time it was programmed.
